title: Fall of a bound pair of two bodies in a sharp field

key_results.statement: Exactly and for all $\lambda$, for the contract $C$ of the question and a field that starts in $\varphi$ with $\Phi\varphi=\gamma\varphi$, $C_f\varphi=e_f\varphi$ (derived for this start, not claimed for another one): $C(\Psi\otimes\varphi)=((C_{\rm red}+e_f)\Psi)\otimes\varphi$ with $C_{\rm red}=\sum_i[A_i+\sum_xP^{(i)}_x\otimes(1+g_ix)G_i+\kappa\hat x_i\otimes X]+U$, the contract of an admissible description of $b_1,b_2,c$; a binding with a factor of the field, $U'\otimes\Phi'$, is not a sum of pair terms and would need a three-object term that (1.10) does not contain iff $\Phi'\notin\mathbb C\mathbb 1_f$ and $U'\neq u_1\otimes\mathbb 1+\mathbb 1\otimes u_2$; in the scalar case $\Phi'=c\,\mathbb 1_f$ it is the admissible pair term $cU'$ of the two bodies, in the reducible case the two admissible pair terms $u_i\otimes\Phi'$ of a body and the field; a non-zero binding of the class $\mathcal W$ on a chain with $L>R$ is not reducible.

Exactly, with the medium in $\chi$ and the field in $\varphi$: $C_{\rm bod}=C^{\rm D}_1+C^{\rm D}_2+U+\sum_ig_i\hat x_i\otimes G_i+\kappa\langle X\rangle(\hat x_1+\hat x_2)$, fixed by $C$, $\chi$, $\varphi$ up to an additive constant; $g_1$, $g_2$, $\kappa\langle X\rangle$, as the coefficients read from $C_{\rm bod}$, are fixed by it and well defined (the argument uses the label 0 of the two types and the finite range of $W$), while the listed numbers $\gamma\theta_i$ and $\kappa\langle\chi\vert X\vert\chi\rangle$ can change under a relisting.

Exactly, on the levels $k_1,k_2$, the gradient terms of $C_{\rm bod}$ are $\hat X_\eta\mathcal K+\hat r\mathcal D_\eta$ with $\mathcal K=g_1M_1\sigma^{(1)}_3+g_2M_2\sigma^{(2)}_3+2\kappa\langle X\rangle$ independent of $\eta$ and $\mathcal D_\eta=\mathcal D_0-\eta\mathcal K$, which depends on $\eta$ iff at least one of the three gradients is non-zero.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$, all data, every bound level, every packet of $\mathcal G(\mathcal P_0)$ and all gradients, at first order in the gradients (fixed $\lambda$, then the long chain; bodies evolving by $C_{\rm bod}$) and for every $\lambda$: the first-order velocities of both parts are $v^{(1)}_i(\lambda)=\lambda\langle\alpha\rangle_g+\rho_i(\lambda)$ with the same coefficient, $\alpha(P)=-E_b''\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P+E_b'\partial_P\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P$.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$, every bound level and every $P$ of its interval, exactly: $\alpha=g_1\alpha_1+g_2\alpha_2+\kappa\langle X\rangle\alpha_X$ with $\alpha_i=-M_i[E_b''\langle\sigma^{(i)}_3\rangle_P-E_b'\partial_P\langle\sigma^{(i)}_3\rangle_P]$ and $\alpha_X=-2E_b''$.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$, every bound level and every packet of $\mathcal G(\mathcal P_0)$, at first order in the gradients: the rest $\rho_i$ of the first-order velocity is given explicitly, with $\rho_i(0)=0$ and $\lvert\rho_i(\lambda)\rvert\le\tau_i\mathsf B_g$ for all $\lambda$, where $\mathsf B_g$ is finite because the level is isolated on the support of $g$ and $g'$ is square integrable; the rests of the two parts differ in the runs of the numerical sets S2–S5 and of S1 with $g_1$ only, within the range of $\lambda$ of each run, and coincide under the exchange symmetry of Step 4.3 (a sufficient condition).

For every binding of $\mathcal W$, every bound level and every packet of $\mathcal G(\mathcal P_0)$, at first order in the gradients: the change of the mean label separation is $\lambda\langle\beta\rangle_g+\sigma(\lambda)$ with bounded $\sigma$ and $\beta=-\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P\partial_P\langle\hat r\rangle_P-2E_b'\,\mathrm{Re}\langle\hat r\psi_P\vert R_P\vert\mathcal K\psi_P\rangle$; there is no term in $\lambda^2$; $\beta\equiv0$ if $W(-r)^{*}=W(r)$ (a sufficient condition), in particular for every diagonal on-site binding; without it $\langle\beta\rangle_g\neq0$ for the numerical level of the control set S5, with no analytic example; whether the bounded change converges for $\lambda\to\infty$ is not derived.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$ and every bound level, at first order in the gradients, on the class $\mathcal S(P_0,I)$ of packet sequences (supports in one compact interval, mean $P_0$, $\delta P\to0$, phase free): with the window average first and the sharp-total-label limit second both limits exist, and the drift acceleration of both parts at $P_0$ is $g_1\alpha_1(P_0)+g_2\alpha_2(P_0)+\kappa\langle X\rangle\alpha_X(P_0)$ with $\alpha_i=-M_i[E_b''\partial_{M_i}E_b-E_b'\partial_{M_i}E_b']$, $\alpha_X=-2E_b''$; the other order exists and agrees with the defining order for every member with $g_1=g_2=0$; for the levels of items 3 and 4 at $P_0=0$ (small $\epsilon$, a fixed $\mathcal P_0$) it exists and agrees iff $g_1=g_2=0$ and does not exist otherwise; for the other members the conditions are (13.28) (necessary and sufficient at a fixed window), (13.29) (necessary; carried by the phase construction of (13.28), analyticity in $\lambda$ and a vanishing mean) and (13.31) (sufficient), and a member with the necessary condition without the sufficient one is excluded where the level has no mirror pair (13.32) and is neither shown to exist nor excluded elsewhere.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$ and every bound level, with the common gradient $g_1=g_2$, exactly at first order in the gradients: the coefficient of the common gradient is $-E_b''\mathcal M_P+E_b'\mathcal M_P'$ with $\mathcal M_P=M_1\langle\sigma^{(1)}_3\rangle_P+M_2\langle\sigma^{(2)}_3\rangle_P=E_b-\langle A_1\rangle_P-\langle A_2\rangle_P-\langle U\rangle_P$: of the terms of the scaling relation only the rest terms enter, through $\mathcal M_P$ and $\mathcal M_P'$, next to the factors $E_b''$ and $E_b'$; the motion terms and the binding term do not enter $\mathcal M_P$.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, the level (11.12) and $P_0=0$, at first order in the gradients: at leading order in $\mathsf R$ and fixed $u$ the drift acceleration of the pair from rest is $a_{\rm pair}=\frac{\varsigma}{\sqrt{1+u^2}}\frac{g_1M_1+g_2M_2+2\kappa\langle X\rangle}{\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2}$, with a relative remainder $O(\epsilon^2)$ on each of the three coefficients that is not uniform in $u$ (where the leading terms cancel in the sum, $a_{\rm pair}$ is given by these remainders and is of order $\epsilon^4$ times the gradients); the exact form is $a_{\rm pair}=-\langle\mathcal K\rangle_0/\mathfrak m_b$, and at leading order it is $-\varsigma(1+u^2)^{-1/2}$ times the inertia-weighted mean $\bar a$ of the free falls.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, the level (11.12) and $P_0=0$: ordered limits of the leading coefficient of $a_{\rm pair}$ (first $\epsilon\to0$ at fixed $u$, then $u$ through the binding): $a_{\rm pair}\to-\varsigma\bar a[1-u^2/2+O(u^4)]$ for $u\to0$ and $a_{\rm pair}\to-\varsigma(\bar a/u)[1+O(u^{-2})]\to0$ for $u\to\infty$.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, the level (11.12) and $P_0=0$, at leading order in $\mathsf R$: $a_{\rm pair}=\varsigma(g_1M_1+g_2M_2+2\kappa\langle X\rangle)/h$ with $h=\sqrt{(\mathfrak m_1+\mathfrak m_2)^2+16w^2\mathfrak m_1^2\mathfrak m_2^2}$ and the additive remainder $O(\epsilon^2)(\lvert g_1\rvert M_1+\lvert g_2\rvert M_2+2\kappa\lvert\langle X\rangle\rvert)/h$, which is a relative $O(\epsilon^2)$ only where the leading terms do not cancel; at a fixed binding $w_{11}\neq0$ its leading coefficient is the same for all pairs of clock levels iff $g_1=g_2=0$ and $\kappa\langle X\rangle=0$ (no fall), so that with a non-zero gradient the falls of two pairs of levels differ for small $\epsilon$; in the ordered wide-pair limit the leading coefficient is the same for all pairs of levels iff $\langle X\rangle=0$ and $\tau_1^2g_1=\tau_2^2g_2$; no statement is made for pairs of levels compared at one common $u$.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, the level (11.12) and $\langle X\rangle=0$, at zeroth order in the gradients and leading order in $\kappa$, under the conditions and in the range of $\lambda$ of (11.19), the rate parameter of the clock of the part $i$ of a pair at rest at the label $x_0$ (the number that multiplies $\lambda$ in the advance of (11.19)) is $r_i(x_0)=\frac{1+g_ix_0}{\lambda_{0,i}}\Gamma_i(x_0)$ with $\Gamma_i=1-\frac{\tau_i^2}{4n_i^2\bar M_i^2}\Lambda(x_0)+O(\epsilon^4)$ at fixed $u$, $n_i=1+g_ix_0$, where $\Lambda(x_0)$ is taken with the clock data of the part $i$ (mean rest cost $\bar M_i$ of the part that is read, level of the other part), so that $\Lambda(0)=\Lambda_{[i]}$ and not $\Lambda$ of (13.13); it is a statement on the rate parameter, not on a rate inferred from readings: (13.35) is the hierarchy under which two upper bounds allow its term of order $\epsilon^2$ to be separated from the remainder of (11.19), and no positive or negative statement on the resolution of that term by a reading is made.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, the level (11.12) and $\langle X\rangle=0$, to first order in the gradients and at fixed $u$, with the clock data of the part $i$ (label $[i]$, $j\neq i$), the relative change per label of the rate parameter is $\varrho_i=g_i+\frac{\tau_i^2}{4\bar M_i^2}[2\Lambda_{[i]}g_i+\frac{\varsigma u_{[i]}^2}{(1+u_{[i]}^2)^{3/2}}\frac{g_ia_{i[i]}+g_ja_j}{a_{[i]}}]+O(\epsilon^4)(\lvert g_1\rvert+\lvert g_2\rvert)$, equal to $g_i$ at leading order; it is derived from (13.21) and (13.22), whose remainder rests on the uniform estimate of Step 7.2, and it is a statement on the rate parameter, not on a rate inferred from the readings of one pair in the field.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, the level (11.12), $P_0=0$, $\langle X\rangle=0$, the common gradient $g_{\rm c}\neq0$ and $\tau_1=\tau_2=\tau$: the pair obeys the relation of the form (4.24), with the relative change $\varrho_i$ of the rate parameter of either part and with $v_{\max}^2$ replaced by $-\varsigma v_{\max}^2/\sqrt{1+u^2}$ ($u$ of the level data), up to a relative $O(\epsilon^2)$ at fixed $u$; with the speed $\tau d_0$ itself it holds neither exactly nor at the leading non-zero order $\epsilon^2$ at a fixed $u$ (both sides vanish through the orders $\epsilon^0$ and $\epsilon^1$; the absolute deviation is of order $\epsilon^2$, the relative deviation $-\Lambda$ of order $\epsilon^0$), for $w_{11}<0$ only in the ordered wide-pair limit, with the leading deviation $-u^2/2$, and not at all for $w_{11}>0$, where the factor is negative at every $u$; for $g_{\rm c}=0$ both sides vanish and the relation holds trivially with any speed.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, the level (11.12) and $\langle X\rangle=0$, to first order in the gradients and without the expansion in $\mathsf R$, $\varrho_i=g_i+\Gamma_i^{-1}\sum_{j}g_jM_j\,\partial^2E_b(0)/\partial M_j\partial M_i$, because $\Gamma_i=\partial E_b(0)/\partial M_i$ and the data at the label $x_0$ are $(1+g_jx_0)M_j$; it is exact in the data as an identity for the rate parameter, not for a rate inferred from readings, which (11.19) fixes only within its remainder.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$ and the level (11.12), in $\mathsf R$ at fixed $u$, $\partial^2E_b(0)/\partial M_j\partial M_i=\delta_{ij}\frac{2a_i}{M_i^2}\Lambda+\frac{a_ia_j}{M_iM_j}\frac{\varsigma u^2}{a(1+u^2)^{3/2}}+O(\epsilon^4)$, from (11.12) differentiated twice in $M_1,M_2$; the remainder is bounded by Cauchy's estimate on a complex neighbourhood of the rest costs whose size does not depend on $\epsilon$, obtained from (11.11) with the statement of its Step 7 and standard analytic perturbation theory, with constants that are not uniform in $u$.

u_i^{-1}$ of order $\epsilon^{-2}$; it contains the binding, the levels of both parts and the mean rest cost $ ar M_i$; it is formed with the rate parameter.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, the level (11.12), $P_0=0$, $\langle X\rangle=0$ and $g_1=g_2\neq0$, at fixed $u$: $\mathsf w_1^2/\mathsf w_2^2=\varrho_2/\varrho_1=1+\frac{\tau_2^2}{4\bar M_2^2}\mathsf y(u_{[2]})-\frac{\tau_1^2}{4\bar M_1^2}\mathsf y(u_{[1]})+O(\epsilon^4)$ with $\mathsf y(u)=2+\varsigma(2+3u^2)(1+u^2)^{-3/2}>0$; the two numbers are the same at relative order $\epsilon^2$ iff $\tau_1^2\mathsf y(u_{[1]})/\bar M_1^2=\tau_2^2\mathsf y(u_{[2]})/\bar M_2^2$, which reduces to $\tau_1/\bar M_1=\tau_2/\bar M_2$ for $u_{[1]}=u_{[2]}$ and in the ordered limits $u\to\infty$ (both signs) and $u\to0$ ($w_{11}>0$); a statement on the rate parameters of the two clocks.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$, every bound level and every packet of $\mathcal G(\mathcal P_0)$, at first order in the gradients: the rest $\dot\rho_i(\lambda)$ of the first-order acceleration is the derivative of (13.9), given explicitly, with $\lvert\dot\rho_i(\lambda)\rvert\le\frac12\tau_i\Gamma_g\mathsf B_g$ for all $\lambda$; its decay for $\lambda\to\infty$ is neither derived nor excluded.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$ and every bound level, at first order in the gradients: at a fixed window $[\lambda_1,\lambda_1+\Lambda]$ the average of the first-order acceleration is $\langle\alpha\rangle_g+\Lambda^{-1}[\langle\mathsf G_i\rangle_g+2\int\mathrm dP\,\mathsf j_g\mathsf f_i]$ with the phase term $\mathsf j_g=\mathrm{Im}(g^{*}g')$ of the packet and $\mathsf f_i(P)=\mathrm{Re}[F_{i,\lambda_1+\Lambda}(P)-F_{i,\lambda_1}(P)]$; on the class $\mathcal S(P_0,I)$, which leaves the phase of the packets free, its limit $\delta P\to0$ exists for every sequence iff $\mathsf f_i\equiv0$ on $\mathcal P_0$ (necessary and sufficient; the necessity by a phase factor on the packets), and it is then $\alpha(P_0)+\mathsf G_i(P_0)/\Lambda$; a zero of $\mathsf f_i$ at $P_0$ alone is not sufficient.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$ and every bound level, with $c_i(\lambda;P)=\mathrm{Re}\langle V_i\psi_P\vert R_Pe^{-i(H(P)-E_b(P))\lambda}\vert\mathcal K\psi_P\rangle$: the other order of the limits (sharp total label first) exists on $\mathcal S(P_0,I)$ only if $c_i\equiv0$ on $\mathbb R\times\mathcal P_0$ (a necessary condition, carried by the criterion (13.28) for all large windows, the analyticity of $c_i$ in $\lambda$ and its vanishing mean), where $c_i(0;P)=-\frac12\partial_P\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P$ and $\partial_\lambda^2c_i(0;P)=-\frac12\langle[V_i,[H(P),\mathcal K]]\rangle_P$; every member with $c_i\not\equiv0$ has no other order, in particular whenever $\langle\mathcal K\rangle_P$ is not constant on $\mathcal P_0$.

For a binding that commutes with $\mathcal K$ (every diagonal binding), $\partial_\lambda^2c_i(0;P)=-g_iM_i\tau_i^2\,\mathrm{Im}\langle\sigma^{(i)}_3\mathsf T_i^2\rangle_P$, and for the level (11.12) $\mathrm{Im}\langle\sigma^{(i)}_3\mathsf T_i^2\rangle_P=-\varsigma a_j\sin2P/\sqrt{w^2+j(P)^2}+O(\epsilon)$ with $j\neq i$; hence, for the levels of items 3 and 4 at $P_0=0$, small $\epsilon$ and a fixed $\mathcal P_0$, the other order of the limits exists on $\mathcal S(P_0,I)$ iff $g_1=g_2=0$.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$ and every bound level, with the complex spectral measure $
u_{i,P}(S)=\langle V_i\psi_P\vert Q_P\mathbb 1_S(H(P)-E_b(P))\vert\mathcal K\psi_Pangle$: $c_i(\lambda;P)=\mathrm{Re}\int\omega^{-1}e^{-i\omega\lambda}\,\mathrm d
u_{i,P}$ and $F_{i,\lambda}(P)=\int\omega^{-1}(1-e^{-i\omega\lambda})\,\mathrm d
u_{i,P}$; the necessary condition $c_i\equiv0$ holds iff $
u_{i,P}(S)=\overline{
u_{i,P}(-S)}$ for all $S$ (iff $\mathrm{Re}F_{i,\lambda}\equiv0$), and a sufficient condition for the other order of the limits on $\mathcal S(P_0,I)$ is $F_{i,\lambda}\equiv0$ on $\mathcal P_0$ for all $\lambda$ (iff $
u_{i,P}=0$), under which the other order agrees with the defining order.

For every binding of $\mathcal W$ and every bound level that has no mirror pair at one $P_1\in\mathcal P_0$ (no two points $E,E'$ of the rest of the spectrum of $H(P_1)$ with $E+E'=2E_b(P_1)$): the other order of the limits exists on $\mathcal S(P_0,I)$ iff $c_i\equiv0$ on $\mathbb R\times\mathcal P_0$ iff $F_{i,\lambda}\equiv0$ on $\mathcal P_0$ for all $\lambda$, and it then agrees with the defining order; a member with the necessary condition and without the sufficient one is excluded there, and is neither shown to exist nor excluded where the level has a mirror pair at every $P\in\mathcal P_0$.

For $(g_1,g_2)\neq(0,0)$, every binding of $\mathcal W$ and all data, $\psi_P$ is an eigenvector of $\mathcal K$ at no $P$ with $0<\lvert P\rvert<\pi$: in a sector $\Sigma\psi_P=s\psi_P$ the eigenvalue equation gives $\frac i2[B\psi_P(r+1)-B^{\dagger}\psi_P(r-1)]=-\frac12(1-s\Sigma)W(r)\psi_P(r)$ with a normal invertible $B$, which forces $\psi_P\equiv0$; hence the eigenvector form $Q_P\mathcal K\psi_P=0$ of the sufficient condition holds on $\mathcal P_0$ iff $g_1=g_2=0$.

For a diagonal on-site binding with $\hat w_{11}\neq0$, the level (11.12), $P_0=0$, $\langle X\rangle=0$, $g_1=g_2=g_{\rm c}\neq0$ and $\tau_1=\tau_2=\tau$, at a fixed $u$: $a_{\rm pair}-a^{(i)}=-\Lambda a^{(i)}(1+O(\epsilon^2))=\Lambda\tau^2g_{\rm c}(1+O(\epsilon^2))$ and $a_{\rm pair}/a^{(i)}-1=-\Lambda(1+O(\epsilon^2))$ with $\Lambda=1+\varsigma/\sqrt{1+u^2}\in(0,2)$; the absolute difference is of order $\epsilon^2$, the order of the falls themselves, and the relative difference of order $\epsilon^0$; the pair and its parts agree trivially through the orders $\epsilon^0$ and $\epsilon^1$ and differ at the leading non-zero order $\epsilon^2$; the first form holds whenever the free parts fall alike.

A statement on two upper bounds, for the reading of the clock label of the part $i$ in the setting of (13.17): a term $\delta r$ of the rate parameter changes the distribution $P_{N_i}$ by less than $2\pi\lvert\delta r\rvert\lambda$, and (11.19) bounds its remainder from above by $\bar{\mathcal R}_i$, the sum of its $O$-terms; the two bounds allow the term to be separated from the remainder where $\lvert\delta r\rvert\lambda\gg\bar{\mathcal R}_i$, which for the term of order $\epsilon^2$ of (13.17) is $\epsilon^2\ell\gg\delta_i^2(1+\ell)^2+\delta P^2(1+\ell)+\kappa$ with $\ell=\lambda/\lambda_{0,i}$, that is $\delta_i\ll\epsilon$, $\delta P\ll\epsilon$ and $\max(\kappa,\delta_i^2,\delta P^2)/\epsilon^2\ll\ell\ll\epsilon^2/\delta_i^2$; this hierarchy is neither necessary nor sufficient for a reading to resolve the term: where it fails the remainder can still be smaller than its bound, and where it holds a positive statement needs in addition a lower bound $\varkappa$ on $\lvert\partial_\vartheta P_{N_i}\rvert$ between the two advances (the sensitivity, which vanishes at an integer advance), with which the term is separated as soon as $\varkappa\lvert\delta r\rvert\lambda>\bar{\mathcal R}_i$; for a term $\delta\varrho$ of $\varrho_i$ and two pairs without gradients at labels $\Delta x$ apart, $\epsilon^2$ is replaced by $\lvert\delta\varrho\rvert\Delta x$; for the readings of one pair in the field no statement is made.

open_issues: The second order in the gradients and the range of λ over which the first order describes the motion are not estimated; (13.9) and (13.10) bound first-order terms only.

Item 2(c), the other order of the limits, for the members with (g1, g2) ≠ (0, 0) other than the levels of items 3 and 4: a member with the necessary condition (N) and without the sufficient condition (S) is excluded where the level has no mirror pair at one P1 (13.32), and is neither shown to exist nor excluded where the level has a mirror pair at every P of the interval (Step 5.3 (iii), with the reason); no member with (g1, g2) ≠ (0, 0) that satisfies (N) is exhibited; the class S(P0, I) leaves the phase of the packets free and no statement is made for a class that restricts it; a classification of the members between (N) and (S) and the evaluation of the other order are outside the scope of the question.
A binding of the class W with β not identically zero is exhibited numerically (set S5), not analytically; the same holds for a level with E_b'(0) ≠ 0 (Step 5.4).

The remainders of (13.13)–(13.20), (13.23)–(13.26), (13.34) and (13.36) (a relative O(ε²), or O(ε⁴) against terms of order ε² in (13.17), (13.18) and (13.26)) are not determined (for the sets S1–S3 with τ/M ≤ 0.2: numerically up to 4 % for (13.13) and up to 7 % for (13.22)) and are not uniform in u.

The first-order corrections to the clock reading of a pair in the field (the gradient across the packet) are not derived; for this reason (13.18) and (13.24)–(13.26) are statements on the rate parameter only, as far as the readings of one pair in the field are concerned; whether a reading resolves a term of order ε² of the rate parameter is not decided: (13.35) is a hierarchy on two upper bounds, and its constants (those of the remainder of (11.19)), a lower bound on that remainder and the sensitivity of the reading distribution at a given advance are not computed, so neither a positive nor a negative statement on resolution is made.
The results hold for a binding and for motion terms without a factor of the field; whether another admissible coupling makes the pair fall like its parts is outside this package.

The remainder O(ε⁴) of (13.22) rests on the uniform estimate of Step 7.2: the reduction (11.11) of 11-bound-pair, extended to complex rest costs by standard analytic perturbation theory; it is an argument at the physicist-formal standard, its constants are not computed and are not bounded for u → 0 or u → ∞; the numerical check finds the scaling ε⁴ for the sets S1–S3 at three scales; (13.24)–(13.26) and the place of the member ϱ_i = 0 use the values (13.22) and share this estimate.

Whether the rest of the first-order acceleration decays for λ → ∞ at a fixed packet is not derived (Step 5.1); the drift acceleration does not need it. Likewise, whether the bounded first-order separation of Step 4.2 converges for λ → ∞ is not derived.
